answers.rationale: For Kara’s solo travel, the repeated pattern is to select available standard no-fee window seats and decline paid seats solely for a more forward window. With no newer seat instruction, free windows should be exhausted before using aisles or paid preferred seats.
Kara consistently prefers standard free windows on solo trips, rather than forward aisles or waiting for check-in. There is no updated instruction that would override that standing preference.

A 68-minute same-terminal connection with no checked bags does not justify overriding Kara’s established free-window preference. She has accepted window seating even on a 58-minute connection and has repeatedly chosen no-fee windows over forward or paid alternatives.

For trips with a partner, Kara explicitly prioritizes adjacent seats over a window and does not want the pair split. They repeatedly selected free adjacent pairs rather than paying for upgraded window-adjacent seating, so the free 20B/20C pair is the best checkout instruction.
